_meta.description: Point-in-time state AI governance and transparency record. Populated entries must cite official state sources; Unknown rows are launch scaffolding for future official-source review.
_meta.scopeNote: Planning and reference aid only. Entries summarize official state public records located for this project; they do not determine legal applicability, compliance status, or whether an agency has fully disclosed every AI use.

federalContext.title: Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence
federalContext.summary: The federal-versus-state AI governance picture is in flux. EO 14365 was signed on December 11, 2025 and published on December 16, 2025, and directs a national AI policy framework review that may affect state AI laws and disclosure requirements.

mandates.instrument: Executive order and task force report
mandates.title: Executive Order 738 and GenAI Task Force Final Report
mandates.citation: Governor of Alabama, Executive Order 738 and GenAI Task Force final report release
mandates.summary: Alabama created a state Task Force on Generative AI through Executive Order 738, and the Governor's Office later released the task force final report covering responsible GenAI use, data ownership, procurement, and executive-branch inventory considerations.

mandates.title: Official record not populated
mandates.summary: Launch scaffold row; no official state AI governance or transparency instrument has been populated in this dataset yet.

mandates.title: P2000: Generative AI Policy
mandates.citation: Arizona Strategic Enterprise Technology Office, P2000 Generative AI Policy
mandates.summary: Arizona publishes a statewide Generative AI policy for state government use, paired with a use procedure that addresses acceptable use, human oversight, privacy, and data-governance expectations for state employees.

mandates.title: AI and Analytics Center of Excellence and statewide AI acceptable-use policy
mandates.citation: Office of the Governor of Arkansas, AI and Analytics Center of Excellence Government Effectiveness and Safety reports (2025-2026)
mandates.summary: A Governor-launched AI and Analytics Center of Excellence delivered Government Effectiveness and Safety reports recommending a Chief AI Officer and NIST-based evaluation of AI systems. A statewide AI acceptable-use policy has been approved for implementation, starting at the Department of Shared Administrative Services, with a chief AI officer hire underway.

mandates.title: Executive Order N-5-26: Trusted AI Procurement
mandates.citation: Executive Department, State of California, Executive Order N-5-26
mandates.summary: California directs state procurement and technology agencies to recommend AI vendor certifications, share responsible AI procurement and adoption practices, expand vetted GenAI access and training for state workers, update the State Digital Strategy, pilot AI-supported government-service access, publish a data minimization toolkit, and issue watermarking guidance.

mandates.title: SB24-205: Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence
mandates.citation: Colorado General Assembly, SB24-205 session law
mandates.summary: Colorado enacted SB24-205, establishing duties for developers and deployers of high-risk artificial intelligence systems and requiring reasonable care to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination.

mandates.title: Public Act No. 23-16: Artificial Intelligence, Automated Decision-Making and Personal Data Privacy
mandates.citation: Connecticut Public Act No. 23-16
mandates.summary: Connecticut requires executive-branch and judicial-branch inventories of AI systems, public posting of those inventories, policies and procedures for AI development, procurement, implementation, use and ongoing assessment, and impact assessments before covered AI systems are implemented.

mandates.title: Delaware Artificial Intelligence Commission (HB 333)
mandates.citation: Delaware House Bill 333 (2024); Del. Code Title 29, Chapter 90C, Subchapter IV
mandates.summary: Creates the Delaware AI Commission within the Department of Technology and Information to recommend statewide AI processes and guidelines for executive, legislative, and judicial agencies and to conduct an inventory of all generative AI usage across the three branches. The Commission reports annually and operates an official site at ai.delaware.gov.

mandates.title: Mayor's Order 2024-028: DC AI Values and AI Strategic Benchmarks
mandates.citation: Government of the District of Columbia, Mayor's Order 2024-028 (February 8, 2024)
mandates.summary: Articulates six AI values that District agencies must clear before deploying any AI tool, establishes an Advisory Group on AI Values Alignment and an OCTO-run AI Taskforce, and phases agency-specific AI strategic plans in cohorts through October 1, 2026.

mandates.title: Official record not populated

mandates.title: Enterprise AI Responsible Use Policy (PS-23-001) and AI Responsible Use Standard (SS-23-002)
mandates.citation: Georgia Technology Authority, Enterprise AI Responsible Use Policy PS-23-001 and AI Responsible Use Standard SS-23-002
mandates.summary: GTA-led enterprise framework requiring executive branch agencies to submit AI tools for GTA review and approval before procurement and deployment, with the AI Responsible Use Standard effective December 1, 2024. Georgia also operates an Office of Artificial Intelligence, an AI Advisory Council, a Chief Digital and AI Officer role, and the Horizons Innovation Lab.

mandates.title: S1227 (2026): Artificial intelligence in public education framework
mandates.citation: Idaho S1227 (2026 session)
mandates.summary: Statewide framework for AI use in Idaho public education: the State Department of Education must issue AI guidance, districts must adopt AI policies, and vendors must disclose AI functionality. Scope note: this governs government AI use in the education sector only; no general executive branch AI instrument was found for Idaho.

mandates.title: Public Act 104-0538: Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act
mandates.citation: Illinois General Assembly, SB0315 / Public Act 104-0538
mandates.summary: Illinois enacted the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act as Public Act 104-0538. The law creates duties for large frontier developers, including frontier AI frameworks, transparency reports, safety-incident reporting, annual independent third-party audits, and whistleblower protections. It is effective January 1, 2027.

mandates.title: State of Indiana Artificial Intelligence Policy and Guidance
mandates.citation: Office of the Indiana Chief Data Officer, State of Indiana AI Policy and Guidance
mandates.summary: Indiana has adopted an enterprise policy for AI use within state government. State employees may use only AI systems assessed and approved by the Office of the Chief Data Officer; agencies submit AI Readiness Assessment materials before implementation or use, and approved exceptions are reevaluated annually.

mandates.title: State of Iowa Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy (ENTERPRISE PY-AI)
mandates.citation: Iowa Department of Management, Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy ENTERPRISE PY-AI, effective March 31, 2025
mandates.summary: Enterprise generative AI policy for supported entities: freely available AI tools are prohibited without prior written DOM approval, AI procurement must use standard state contract clauses and DOM consultation, AI-generated code must be identified and risk-assessed, and human fallback systems are required where AI fails. Entities remain accountable for decisions and materials produced with AI.

mandates.title: Senate Substitute for HB 2313: AI platforms of concern prohibition
mandates.citation: 2025 Session Laws of Kansas, Chapter 84 (Senate Substitute for House Bill 2313)
mandates.summary: Prohibits state agency devices and state networks from accessing AI platforms of concern, including DeepSeek and models controlled by countries of concern, and requires agencies to deactivate and delete existing accounts. Exceptions exist for law enforcement and cybersecurity investigations.

mandates.title: SB 4 (2025): Government AI governance under KRS 42.720 to 42.742
mandates.citation: Kentucky Acts Ch. 66 (2025), Senate Bill 4; KRS 42.722, 42.726, and a new section of KRS 42.720 to 42.742
mandates.summary: Requires the Commonwealth Office of Technology to establish AI policy standards and creates the Artificial Intelligence Governance Committee, with ISO/IEC 42001-aligned standards, a centralized AI system registry, agency approval requirements, and public disclosure of AI use. Signed March 24, 2025 with an emergency clause, effective immediately.

mandates.title: EO JML 25-103, amended by JML 25-109: State Government's Use of AI
mandates.citation: La. Executive Order JML 25-103 (2025), amended by JML 25-109; OTS Artificial Intelligence Acceptable Use Policy
mandates.summary: Governor's order on state government AI use: agency AI use requires CIO approval (or agency head outside OTS scope), OTS must inventory all AI contracts, restricted data may not enter AI systems, and a temporary procurement pause ran to December 15, 2025. OTS followed with a statewide AI Acceptable Use Policy barring AI from independently making business decisions and requiring labeling of AI-generated content.

mandates.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy
mandates.citation: Maine Office of Information Technology, Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy
mandates.summary: MaineIT publishes a Generative Artificial Intelligence policy for state users, documenting acceptable-use expectations and controls for state use of GenAI tools after earlier cybersecurity directives paused unsanctioned use.

mandates.title: Catalyzing the Responsible and Productive Use of Artificial Intelligence in Maryland State Government
mandates.citation: Governor of Maryland, Artificial Intelligence Executive Order
mandates.summary: Maryland establishes principles for AI use in state agencies, including fairness and equity, innovation, privacy, safety, transparency, accountability, and human-centered government service. The order establishes an AI Subcabinet to develop and implement a comprehensive AI action plan and guardrails for agency use.

mandates.title: Executive Order No. 629: Establishing an Artificial Intelligence Strategic Task Force
mandates.citation: Commonwealth of Massachusetts Executive Order No. 629
mandates.summary: Massachusetts established an AI Strategic Task Force to study AI and generative AI impacts on the state, including effects on state employees, constituents, private business, and higher education, collect stakeholder input, and advise the Governor and executive branch through a written report.

mandates.title: DTMB Adoption and Usage of Artificial Intelligence: Guidelines and Responsibilities
mandates.citation: Michigan Department of Technology, Management and Budget, Adoption and Usage of Artificial Intelligence Guidelines and Responsibilities
mandates.summary: Statewide DTMB guidance requiring any external AI tool that stores, analyzes, or processes state data to obtain an Authority to Operate through the Michigan Security Accreditation Process, with centralized AI governance and intake through a DTMB AI Core Team. Michigan has deployed generative AI chatbots on Michigan.gov and MiLogin in phased rollouts.

mandates.title: Public Artificial Intelligence Services Security Standard
mandates.citation: Minnesota IT Services, Public Artificial Intelligence Services Security Standard
mandates.summary: Minnesota's AI security standard guides responsible use of public AI services by state employees and applies to employees, contractors, and third parties who develop, deploy, or use AI systems and applications within state government. It focuses on secure use, productivity, and protection of private, sensitive, or protected data.

mandates.title: EO 1584 (2025) and ITS Acceptable Use Policy for Artificial Intelligence
mandates.citation: Miss. Executive Order No. 1584 (Jan. 8, 2025); Mississippi ITS Acceptable Use Policy for Artificial Intelligence (Nov. 25, 2025)
mandates.summary: Mississippi's first AI executive order directed ITS to inventory all AI in state agencies, evaluate agency AI processes and procurement, and develop responsible use policy recommendations. ITS delivered the statewide AI Acceptable Use Policy framework and published the 2025 State Agency AI Inventory Report; a statutory AI Regulation Task Force (SB 2406) reports annually to the Legislature.

mandates.title: EO 26-02 (2026): AI strategic framework for Missouri government
mandates.citation: Mo. Executive Order 26-02 (Gov. Kehoe, Jan. 2026)
mandates.summary: Directs the Office of Administration Commissioner to develop a strategic framework for AI integration in Missouri government prioritizing expedited work, improved services, data privacy and security, human decision-making, transparency and accountability, and data quality, plus policy recommendations and AI training best practices. OA has a dedicated head of AI. Reported tier: confirmed via secondary coverage; capture the governor.mo.gov EO PDF to promote to Verified.

mandates.title: HB 178 (2025): Government use of artificial intelligence, MCA Title 2, Chapter 21
mandates.citation: 2025 Montana Laws, Chapter 427 (HB 178); Mont. Code Ann. Title 2, Chapter 21, Part 1
mandates.summary: Prohibits government entities and state officers from using AI for cognitive manipulation, discriminatory classification, or broad surveillance, with narrow exceptions. Requires disclosure when AI is used in public interfaces or published materials, and human review with power to modify or reject any AI recommendation or decision affecting a person's rights.

mandates.title: NITC Standard 8-609: Artificial Intelligence
mandates.citation: Nebraska Information Technology Commission, Technical Standards and Guidelines 8-609
mandates.summary: Statewide standards for AI systems owned, used, or managed by the State of Nebraska: mandatory consultation with the OCIO security risk team, privacy and third-party risk assessments, restrictions on training AI with agency data, and ethics and fairness requirements for AI output.

mandates.title: Policy on the Responsible and Ethical Use of AI in Nevada State Government Executive Branch
mandates.citation: Nevada Governor's Technology Office / OCIO, Policy on the Responsible and Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence in Nevada State Government Executive Branch
mandates.summary: OCIO-owned policy setting minimum standards for AI deployment across the executive branch: OCIO oversees implementation, the State Technology Governance Committee works with an AI Working Group on statewide coordination, and the State Information Security Committee develops the companion AI risk and security policy. Listed on the Governor's Technology Office governance page among current statewide policies.

mandates.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies Policy
mandates.citation: New Hampshire Department of Information Technology, SoNH Use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies Policy
mandates.summary: New Hampshire publishes a state policy for use of artificial intelligence technologies, guided by its AI ethics code and covering responsible use, human oversight, data quality, and agency accountability expectations.

mandates.title: Executive Order No. 346: Artificial Intelligence Task Force
mandates.citation: State of New Jersey Executive Order No. 346
mandates.summary: New Jersey established an Artificial Intelligence Task Force to study emerging AI technologies, issue findings on societal impacts, recommend government actions for ethical and responsible AI use, make its report available to the Legislature and public, and direct state technology and innovation offices to develop AI policy, training, and service-improvement work.

mandates.title: Acceptable Use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies
mandates.citation: New York State Office of Information Technology Services Policy NYS-P25-001
mandates.summary: New York's acceptable-use policy applies to state entity AI systems that could directly impact the public. It requires leadership approval before adopting new AI systems, identification of an information owner, human oversight for public-impacting decisions, documentation of AI-supported decisions and methods, and periodic assessment for reliability, safety, and fairness.

mandates.title: Statewide AI Strategic Roadmap
mandates.citation: North Carolina Department of Information Technology, Statewide AI Strategic Roadmap
mandates.summary: North Carolina publishes a statewide AI strategic roadmap following Executive Order 24, with planning for governance, AI-enabled service delivery, education, workforce development, cybersecurity, and the state AI Accelerator.

mandates.title: NDIT Artificial Intelligence Policy and Guidelines
mandates.citation: North Dakota Information Technology, Artificial Intelligence Guidelines supplementing the NDIT Artificial Intelligence Policy
mandates.summary: Applies to all executive branch state agencies. Establishes an AI risk matrix, requires NDIT Governance, Risk, and Compliance assessment and executive leadership approval for enterprise AI use, and commits the state to consulting NIST guidance. A legislative interim AI and Data Center Committee was announced in mid 2026.

mandates.title: AI in Ohio's Education Model Policy
mandates.citation: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce, AI in Ohio's Education Model Policy
mandates.summary: Ohio publishes an official AI model policy and guidance for education use. This row records the education-sector public record only and does not assert an enterprise-wide state executive-branch AI policy.

mandates.title: AI Task Force and Chief AI and Technology Officer
mandates.citation: State of Oklahoma, AI task force and Chief AI and Technology Officer announcements
mandates.summary: Oklahoma announced an AI task force through the Governor's Office and later announced a state Chief AI and Technology Officer through OMES, establishing public records for state AI coordination and leadership.

mandates.title: Executive Order 23-26 and State Government AI Advisory Council Action Plan
mandates.citation: State of Oregon Executive Order 23-26; State Government AI Advisory Council Final Recommended Action Plan
mandates.summary: Oregon established the State Government AI Advisory Council through Executive Order 23-26 and finalized an action plan to guide state-government AI use, recommending executive actions for AI governance, security frameworks, reference architecture, privacy, workforce readiness, and responsible service delivery.

mandates.title: Executive Order 2023-19: Expanding and Governing the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Technologies Within the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
mandates.citation: Commonwealth of Pennsylvania Executive Order 2023-19
mandates.summary: Pennsylvania establishes a Generative AI Governing Board and statewide governance values for agency use of generative AI. The order directs responsive and responsible standards intended to prevent generative AI use from enabling activities that violate Commonwealth or federal law.

mandates.title: Executive Order 24-06: Artificial Intelligence and Data Centers of Excellence
mandates.citation: State of Rhode Island Executive Order 24-06 (February 29, 2024)
mandates.summary: Establishes the Rhode Island AI Task Force, a Center of Excellence for AI and Data under the Department of Administration and ETSS, a chief data officer role, and a statewide federated data platform. The Task Force assesses AI risks and opportunities and advises state policymakers.

mandates.title: South Carolina State Agencies Artificial Intelligence Strategy (June 2024)
mandates.citation: South Carolina Department of Administration, State Agencies Artificial Intelligence Strategy, June 2024
mandates.summary: Statewide AI strategy for state agencies built on Protect, Promote, Pursue: AI governance policies aligned to the Division of Information Security standards, risk management processes, an AI Center of Excellence, and an AI Advisory Group. Developed by the state CIO and CISO with an AI Workgroup spanning 80 plus agencies; OTIS and DIS execute the roadmap.

mandates.title: Tennessee Artificial Intelligence Advisory Council Act and Enterprise AI Policy
mandates.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. Title 4, Chapter 3, Part 31 (HB 2325, 2024; amended 2025); Tennessee Enterprise Artificial Intelligence Policy 200-POL-007
mandates.summary: Statutory AI Advisory Council co-chaired by the Finance and Administration Commissioner and the state CIO, paired with a NIST AI RMF-aligned Enterprise AI Policy and an AI Review Committee gating AI solutions. The Council's December 2025 action plan includes the state's first statewide inventory of government AI use cases and an annual statutory reporting requirement.

mandates.title: Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act
mandates.citation: Texas House Bill 149, 89th Legislature, Regular Session
mandates.summary: Texas establishes a regulatory framework for AI systems, including prohibited uses, disclosure and governance requirements, enforcement authority, civil penalties, and a state artificial intelligence council. The enrolled act became effective January 1, 2026.

mandates.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy Act
mandates.citation: Utah Code Title 13, Chapter 72
mandates.summary: Utah creates an Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy and Artificial Intelligence Learning Laboratory Program to study AI risks, benefits, impacts, and policy implications, support consumer education, and allow regulatory mitigation agreements for participants using or seeking to use AI technology in the state.

mandates.title: 3 V.S.A. Chapter 69: Division of Artificial Intelligence
mandates.summary: Establishes a statutory Division of Artificial Intelligence within the Agency of Digital Services to review all AI developed, employed, or procured in state government, with an annually updated state AI code of ethics, an AI Advisory Council, and review of the ADS automated decision systems inventory. The inventory is published, and the 2026 ADS annual report lists live AI systems in production. Effective July 1, 2022.

mandates.title: Commonwealth of Virginia Artificial Intelligence Governance
mandates.citation: Virginia Information Technologies Agency, Artificial Intelligence Governance
mandates.summary: Virginia publishes an AI governance program through VITA, including an enterprise AI registry and review process tied to Executive Order 30 and a Commonwealth AI strategy task force report.

mandates.title: Executive Order 24-01: Artificial Intelligence
mandates.citation: State of Washington Executive Order 24-01
mandates.summary: Washington directs state technology and enterprise services agencies to identify potential generative AI initiatives, create pilot infrastructure, issue public-sector procurement, use, and monitoring guidelines, require NIST AI RMF-aligned governance certification for high-risk generative AI vendors, and develop training for state government workers.

mandates.title: W. Va. Code 5A-6-9: Task Force on Artificial Intelligence
mandates.summary: Creates the West Virginia Task Force on Artificial Intelligence within the Office of the Governor to recommend which agencies should own AI policy, develop public sector AI best practices, and inventory current and proposed AI use within state agencies. The WV Office of Technology publishes responsible use guidance and maintains a list of approved AI tools.

mandates.title: Executive Order 211: Governor's Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence
mandates.citation: Governor of Wisconsin, Executive Order 211
mandates.summary: Wisconsin created the Governor's Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence to study AI's near-term and long-term impacts on Wisconsin workers, employers, and workforce-development needs.
